cond_0001.requirements:
To be eligible for the Recent Graduate Program, applicants must meet one of the following:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
Minimum Requirements
Engineering degree from a school with at least one ABET-accredited program; OR a degree that includes differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials; (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials; (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR combination of college-level education, training, and/or technical experience demonstrating thorough knowledge of physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and a good understanding of engineering sciences and techniques, demonstrated by one of the following: (1) current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE); (2) passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration; (3) at least 60 semester hours of courses in physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences meeting the requirements of an engineering program; (4) a bachelor's degree in a related scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology) plus at least 1 year of professional engineering experience under professional engineering supervision.
For GS-7: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05 level including interpreting or reviewing scientific data; OR one year of graduate-level education related to engineering; OR a qualifying bachelor's degree meeting Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria based on class standing, GPA, or honor society membership; OR a combination of the above experience and education equaling 100%; OR an engineering bachelor's degree with appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician; OR a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07 level including preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis; OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or equivalent; OR a combination of superior academic achievement and 1 year of appropriate specialized engineering experience; OR a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering plus 1 year of appropriate professional engineering experience.
Preferred Requirements
Prior federal service experience
Experience in tobacco product science or regulatory science contexts

cond_0032.intro: [Company name masked] is responsible for planning, managing, directing and coordinating major tobacco program objectives to implement the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. The incumbent serves as a General Engineer in the Office of Science (OS), Division of Product Science (DPS), Engineering Branch. Assignments involve providing comprehensive professional engineering review, analysis, and advice for a variety of difficult problems and issues. Most people become stronger in this kind of engineering review and analysis work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0032.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university.
OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

OR-

OR-

OR-

OR-

OR-

OR-

[Company name masked] is responsible for planning, managing, directing and coordinating major tobacco program objectives to implement the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. The role sits within the Office of Science (OS), Division of Product Science (DPS), Engineering Branch. You will work alongside colleagues to provide professional engineering review, analysis, and advice on a range of difficult problems and issues.
cond_0189.responsibilities: Assignments involve working with the team to provide comprehensive professional engineering review, analysis, and advice for a variety of difficult problems and issues. You will coordinate with colleagues across the division to support the implementation of tobacco program objectives and help ensure scientific and engineering standards are met.
cond_0189.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Completed all requirements for an associate's, bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR: Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR: Expected to graduate with a qualifying degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
Engineering degree: The program must (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials; (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials; and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics.
OR: Combination of education and experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering, demonstrated by one of the following: (1) Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico; (2) Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration; (3) Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences including the courses specified in the basic requirements; (4) Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology), provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
For GS-7: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data; OR completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position from an accredited college and/or university; OR a bachelor's degree meeting the Basic Qualification Requirements AND Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership; OR a combination of the above experience and education that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements; OR an engineering bachelor's degree AND appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician; OR successful completion of a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
Preferred Requirements
For GS-9: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis; OR 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or a master's or equivalent graduate degree; OR a combination of superior academic achievement AND one year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience; OR successful completion of a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND one year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

cond_0235.intro: [Company name masked] is responsible for planning, managing, directing and coordinating major tobacco program objectives. Assignments involve providing comprehensive professional engineering review, analysis, and advice for a variety of difficult problems and issues.
cond_0235.requirements:
To be eligible for the Recent Graduate Program, applicants must meet one of the following:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
Minimum Requirements
Engineering degree from a school with at least one ABET-accredited program; OR a degree that includes differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials; (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials; (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR combination of college-level education, training, and/or technical experience demonstrating thorough knowledge of physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and a good understanding of engineering sciences and techniques, demonstrated by one of the following: (1) current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE); (2) passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration; (3) at least 60 semester hours of courses in physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences meeting the requirements of an engineering program; (4) a bachelor's degree in a related scientific field (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology) plus at least 1 year of professional engineering experience under professional engineering supervision.
For GS-7: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-05 level including interpreting or reviewing scientific data; OR one year of graduate-level education related to engineering; OR a qualifying bachelor's degree meeting Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.) criteria based on class standing, GPA, or honor society membership; OR a combination of the above experience and education equaling 100%; OR an engineering bachelor's degree with appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician; OR a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9: At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-07 level including preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis; OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or equivalent; OR a combination of superior academic achievement and 1 year of appropriate specialized engineering experience; OR a 5-year program of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering plus 1 year of appropriate professional engineering experience.
Preferred Requirements
Prior federal service experience
Experience in tobacco product science or regulatory science contexts

Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

OR-

OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

cond_0269.intro: [Company name masked] is looking for a General Engineer to join the Office of Science, Division of Product Science, Engineering Branch. The role involves leading professional engineering review, analysis, and advice on a range of difficult technical problems and issues related to tobacco product science.
cond_0269.responsibilities: You will own comprehensive professional engineering review and analysis for a variety of difficult problems and issues. You will execute technical assessments and deliver authoritative engineering advice in support of major tobacco program objectives under the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. You will direct your work within the Engineering Branch to ensure rigorous, science-based outcomes.
cond_0269.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university.
OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

Prior federal service experience
Experience in tobacco product science or regulatory science contexts

cond_0286.intro:
[Company name masked] is looking for a General Engineer to join the Office of Science, Division of Product Science, Engineering Branch. The role sits within a program focused on tobacco product regulation. The incumbent will carry out professional engineering review, analysis, and advice on a range of technical problems and issues.
This position is filled through the Recent Graduate Program, which provides entry-level federal employment opportunities for recent graduates. Upon successful completion of the program and at the agency's discretion, the appointee may be converted to a term or permanent position in the competitive service.
cond_0286.responsibilities:
Assignments involve:
Conducting professional engineering review and analysis of technical problems and issues
Providing engineering advice based on findings
Supporting program objectives related to tobacco product science
Documenting and sharing results with relevant staff as required by project needs

OR-
E. An engineering bachelor's degree AND appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-

For GS-9:
A. At least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service, which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Two years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering, or a master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. A combination of superior academic achievement AND one year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-

cond_0309.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Recently completed, or are expected to complete by 06/30/2024, an associate's, bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited institution within the past 2 years — or equivalent release from active military duty within that window.
Engineering degree (or equivalent background) meeting one of the following paths:
A. A bachelor's degree in engineering from a program accredited by ABET, or a degree that included calculus and courses in at least five of the seven core engineering science areas (statics/dynamics, strength of materials, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, electrical fields and circuits, nature and properties of materials, or a comparable area).
B. A combination of college-level education, training, and technical experience demonstrating thorough knowledge of physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, supported by one of: current EI/EIT registration or PE licensure; passing the FE exam; at least 60 semester hours in physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences; or a related scientific bachelor's degree (e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, computer science, mathematics) with around 1 year of professional engineering experience under supervision.
For GS-7: around 1 year of specialized experience at the GS-5 level (e.g., interpreting or reviewing scientific data), or 1 year of graduate-level education in engineering, or a qualifying bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, or an engineering bachelor's degree with experience as an Engineering Technician, or a 5-year/160-semester-hour engineering program.
For GS-9: around 1 year of specialized experience at the GS-7 level (e.g., preparing scientific progress reports, presentations, or conducting analysis), or 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master's degree in engineering, or a combination of superior academic achievement and 1 year of appropriate engineering experience, or a 5-year/160-semester-hour engineering bachelor's degree plus 1 year of professional engineering experience.
Official transcripts or documentation verifying eligibility and degree/certificate conferment (or anticipated graduation date) are required.
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with interpreting or reviewing scientific data in an engineering context.
Some exposure to preparing technical reports or presentations.
Background in or willingness to obtain professional engineering registration (EI, EIT, or PE).
Openness to working within a structured federal program environment and completing program requirements for potential conversion to a permanent position.

OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

OR-

OR-

OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

cond_0446.requirements:

OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. OR-

OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

OR-

OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university.
OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

Engineering degree from a school with at least one ABET-accredited program; OR a degree that includes differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials; (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials; (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.

OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-

A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-

OR-

Assignments involve providing comprehensive professional engineering review, analysis, and advice for a variety of difficult problems and issues. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of engineering analysis and scientific review the work involves.
cond_0625.requirements:
Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to participate in this Recent Graduate Program:
A. Completed all requirements for an associates, bachelors, masters, professional, doctorate, vocational, or technical degree or qualifying certificate from an accredited educational institution within the 2 years preceding the closing date of this announcement.
OR-
B. Released or discharged from active duty within the previous two years by 04/22/2024, where as a veteran who, due to a military service obligation, was precluded from applying to the Recent Graduate Program during any portion of the 2-year eligibility period following completion of degree or certificate requirements, are entitled to a full 2-year period of eligibility upon release or discharge from active duty. In no event, however, may the eligibility period extend beyond 6 years from the date on which the preference eligible veteran completed the requirements of the degree or certificate.
OR-
C. Individuals who are expected to graduate with a qualifying Associate's, Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, professional, vocational or technical degree or certificate program by 06/30/2024. Current students must meet all eligibility and qualification requirements before a final offer can be made.
NOTE: You must submit transcripts or official documentation to verify your eligibility under the Recent Graduate Program. Transcripts MUST reflect the degree/certificate program and the degree conferred date. If your degree/certificate has not been conferred, you must provide proof of the anticipated graduation date. Selectee's entry on duty date will be upon degree conferment.
In addition to the eligibility requirements for the Pathways Recent Graduate Program, you must also meet the following Individual Occupational Requirements by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801 positions.
A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics.
OR-
B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:
Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university.
OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

A. Degree: Engineering. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

OR-

OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.

Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.
Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico.
Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A.
Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.
In addition to meeting the Individual Occupational Requirements above, you must also meet the OPM Qualification Requirements listed below by 04/22/2024 in order to qualify for the General Engineer, 0801, at GS-7/9.
For GS-7:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the Federal service which includes interpreting or reviewing scientific data.
OR-
B. Completion of one year of graduate level education related to the position being filled (Engineer) from an accredited college and/or university.
OR-
C. A bachelor's degree as described in the Basic Qualification Requirements above AND meet Superior Academic Achievement provision (S.A.A.) criteria. S.A.A. Is based on (1) class standing, (2) grade-point average, or (3) honor society membership.
OR-
D. Have a combination of experience as described in ""A"" above and education as described in ""B"" above, that when combined equals 100% of the total requirements.
OR-
E. Have an engineering bachelor's degree AND have appropriate specialized experience as an Engineering Technician.
OR-
F. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering.
For GS-9:
A. Applicants must have at least one full year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service which includes preparing scientific progress reports, presentations or conducting analysis.
OR-
B. Have 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree in Engineering or master's or equivalent graduate degree.
OR-
C. Have a combination of superior academic achievement AND one (1) year of appropriate specialized Engineering experience.
OR-
D. Have successfully completed a 5-year program of study of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering AND have one (1) year of appropriate professional Engineering experience.
